title: Appendix A — Proposal
text:
Group Members

Ethan De Brauw,
Linnea Joanen
Eli Stottrup
Short Description: Cost-benefit analysis of Pokemon card market
Research Questions: How do markets change over time? What impact do PSA grades have on the card (are some cards worth more ungraded, given that PSA grading is ~$80/card and takes ~6 months to complete)? Are the markets too volatile to make large investments?
Reasons for research: People are becoming increasingly dependent on ‘side hustles,’ especially those surrounding pop culture (sports gambling, labubus, baseball cards) and the Pokemon market is particularly lucrative and in high demand.
Communication method: We will use Google Chat.
Expected response time: 12 hours, with understanding for exceptions.
Meeting time: Wednesday nights ??? Ethan: I am unavailable Wednesdays every week from 7-11, but I can do Tuesdays, Thursdays, Fridays (early afternoon)
Roles: Roles to rotate as we move through the project, researcher(the individual gathering data), connecting with a wrangler, then builder, then looking over the data as a whole group before doing the process again refining it.
Conflict resolution: Direct confrontation of problems head on, discussing with group mates in a timely manner, not letting issues fester, with all members expected to hold themselves accountable and accept responsibility when they make mistakes.
Timeline: Data in and rough viz by Thanksgiving: this is our guiding goal for November. We want to have PM5 done before Thanksgiving. Aim to have PM2 and 3 done by November 6. PM4 by November 13. Two meetings to make PM5 really solid and set up for a good PM6 PM6 week of 11/30 PM7 in the two weeks thereafter

title: Appendix B — Case Study
text:
Your case study go here.
https://pudding.cool/2017/02/new-slang/
In the 2017 Pudding article data visualization was used to tell a story about slang and how it evolves and the geographical and political ties current slang has. The author had taken google search data and compiled it into a set of 43 words from 2013-2016. These words popularity were then charted against each other over time. This search data was then broken further down into geographical regions over time in the next section. A subset of these words within a politcal context are then taken such as WOKE, SJW, TRIGGERED, AND GASLIGHTING. The geographical origins and popularity of these words were taken into account and then cross refrenced with common knowleges of the geographies and political climates of the time period 2016-2017. This offers a story structure as it takes a large set of data and slowly condenses it into separate smaller datasets which are able to have stories and narratives around them.
